prompts.domain_preamble: You are optimizing a CRISPR-Cas9 guide RNA spacer: a 20-nucleotide DNA string that directs Cas9 to a genomic target next to an NGG PAM. The danger is off-target cleavage at other genomic sites that tolerate a few mismatches to the guide. Key biophysics: off-target sites already carry mismatches to the guide, so each substitution you introduce in the editable region compounds the thermodynamic destabilization of those off-target heteroduplexes while the on-target duplex (stabilized by the fixed PAM-proximal seed) tolerates it. You have a tight substitution budget, so spend it on the positions and base changes that most improve specificity and remove genomic off-target sites.
prompts.aggressiveness_text: Optimize ITERATIVELY, like hill-climbing on the best guide so far. Change one substitution at a time: keep edits that lowered the score (better specificity / fewer off-targets) and revert edits that raised it. Reuse your limited budget on the highest-impact positions rather than spreading edits thinly.
prompts.target_description:
Design a CRISPR-Cas9 guide RNA spacer that MINIMIZES off-target cleavage while preserving on-target binding. The score is a thermodynamic composite (CRISPRspec RNA:DNA hybridization specificity, with soft GC-content and homopolymer penalties); lower reported score = better guide. Productive substitutions sit in the PAM-distal mutable region and add thermodynamic mismatch penalties at off-target sites (which already carry mismatches) while the seed region keeps on-target binding intact. Prefer C/G substitutions that create strongly destabilizing mismatches; keep GC in 40-60% and avoid runs of >3 identical bases. Once specificity is maxed, prefer candidates with the fewest genomic off-target sites (reported as n_off_targets).
Budget guidance: you may use up to 4 substitutions, but treat 4 as a ceiling, not a target. In practice the best guides need only 1-2 well-chosen substitutions — a few high-impact edits usually improve specificity while keeping the spacer from accidentally matching new genomic locations, whereas many edits tend to create new off-target sites. Aim for the best result achievable with about 1-2 substitutions; add a 3rd or 4th only when the candidate is clearly still poor (specificity low or many off-targets remain), and prefer to keep the edit count low rather than spending the whole budget.
prompts.bounds_description_example:
- spacer: a 20-letter DNA string over {A,C,G,T} (no U, no N).
- Editable positions: 0..11 (1-indexed 1..12, the PAM-distal 5' region). You may substitute bases ONLY here.
- FIXED positions: 12..19 (the PAM-proximal seed region) must remain exactly 'AATTTTTT'. Changing them is rejected.
- Edit budget: at most 4 substitutions relative to the original guide 'TTTATTAAAAAAAATTTTTT'. Exceeding it is rejected.
- Substitutions only: same length (20), no insertions/deletions.
